details.description: Llama Prompt Guard 2 86M is Meta's larger prompt-attack classifier, built on the mDeBERTa-base architecture with 86 million parameters, that detects prompt injection and jailbreak attempts in text sent to an LLM. Given an input, it labels it as either "benign" or "malicious" rather than generating a reply. Its multilingual base model gives it stronger cross-language attack detection than Meta's smaller 22M variant, at higher latency, and it is meant to run as a safety filter in front of another LLM rather than as a conversational model itself.
advantages: Meta reports an AUC of 0.998 for English-language attack detection and 0.995 for multilingual detection.
Built on mDeBERTa-base, giving stronger multilingual attack detection than the smaller 22M model, per Meta's model card.
Uses adversarial-resistant tokenization intended to counter attacks such as whitespace manipulation, per Meta's model card.
Evaluated by Meta for attack detection across eight languages: English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, and Thai.
disadvantages: Meta states the model remains vulnerable to adaptive attacks.
Higher latency (92.4 ms per classification on an A100 GPU) than the 22M variant, per Meta's model card.
A classifier only: it outputs a benign/malicious label, not a chat completion or explanation.
use_cases: Screening user or tool inputs for prompt injection before they reach a downstream LLM.
Detecting jailbreak attempts in LLM or agent pipelines, including multilingual inputs.
Complementing existing safety measures as an additional filtering layer.
Monitoring production LLM traffic for misuse patterns.

evaluations.name: Attack Prevention Rate (real-world agentic eval, 3% utility reduction)

notes: This is a binary safety classifier (benign/malicious), not a conversational chat model, even though Groq serves it via /v1/chat/completions and the catalog lists kind=chat. Catalog facts (512/512 tokens, text_input/text_output) match the model card. AUC figures (0.998 English, 0.995 multilingual) are on a 0-1 scale so kept out of the 0-100 evaluations list and stated as advantages instead.
